idiom_name: sttp model Uri + uri interpolator + final case class Link envelope
implementation_notes: Scala represents the link as a typed immutable value: the JVM's java.net.URI is always available, and the dominant stacks add typed URI models - sttp.model.Uri (a case class; the uri interpolator mints hrefs with context-aware percent-encoding, Uri.parse is total and returns Either[String, Uri], conversions to and from java.net.URI are provided) plus http4s' org.http4s.Uri and its RFC 8288 header model (headers.Link over NonEmptyList[LinkValue(uri, rel, type)]). The producer/carrier/consumer roles collapse into a small final case class Link(rel: String, href: Uri, method: Method = Method.GET) - an inert value that survives serialization and crosses process boundaries inside JSON payloads; the consumer selects by rel (find/collectFirst) and dereferences late via basicRequest.get(link.href).send(backend), with ResolveRelativeUrisBackend resolving relative references at send time. This replaces the hand-written link grammar, parser, and resolver; the classic form (plain java.net.URI plus hand-built rel-to-href maps) remains justified outside these stacks, where rel/type metadata simply becomes a team convention instead of a checked model.
code_sketch:
final case class Link(rel: String, href: Uri, method: Method = Method.GET)

def paymentLink(order: Order): Link =                 // Link Producer
  Link("payment", uri"/payments/${order.paymentId}") // interpolator percent-encodes

val link = order.links.find(_.rel == "payment").getOrElse(sys.error("no payment link")) // Consumer
val backend = ResolveRelativeUrisBackend(DefaultSyncBackend()) // resolves relative hrefs
val resp   = basicRequest.get(link.href).send(backend)        // dereference = one GET
pitfalls: A received link is inert only if the whole envelope is immutable: re-parse untrusted hrefs with Uri.parse (returns Either[String, Uri]) and keep the carrier case class final with vals - a raw String href or a mutable carrier reintroduces the hand-parsed grammar the typed model replaced, and .get-style unwrapping of the Either turns one malformed link into a NoSuchElementException crash instead of a rejected message.

The typed Uri guarantees well-formedness, not authorization: basicRequest.get(link.href) dereferences whatever absolute authority arrived, so validate the resolved scheme and host against an allowlist before send() and enforce authorization at resolution time - otherwise one rel="next" link turns the service into an SSRF pivot against internal topology.

The uri interpolator escapes embedded segments in context but assumes literal text is already encoded: hand-concatenating pre-encoded strings into the literal part double-escapes ('%20' becomes '%2520'), so build hrefs by interpolation or Uri segment methods, never by string addition.

Link metadata models fragment across stacks: http4s' header model changed shape (v0.20's Link(uri, rel, ...) case class became Link(values: NonEmptyList[LinkValue]) from v0.21) and sttp Uri is a distinct type from java.net.URI despite the provided conversions - carrying links as bare Strings to stay 'stack-neutral' silently drops rel/type, so keep the case-class envelope in the payload and pin library versions for header-level contracts.

variants.name: http4s typed Uri + RFC 8288 Link header model
variants.implementation_notes: In the http4s stack the link target is org.http4s.Uri - a strict RFC 3986 model built with the uri interpolator, path segment appending (base / "payments" / id), or Uri.fromString (total, returning Either); plain strings are rejected by design. The server transfers RFC 8288 links as real header values: headers.Link(LinkValue(uri, rel = Some("payment"), type = Some(MediaType.application.json))) put onto the Response, and the consumer dereferences with an org.http4s.client.Client (Resource-managed, decoded as IO). The model changed across versions - v0.20's Link(uri, rel, title, type) case class became Link(values: NonEmptyList[LinkValue]) from v0.21 - so pin the http4s series wherever the Link header is part of an API contract. Choose this variant over sttp when the server side is already http4s and links must appear in the Link header itself rather than in the body envelope.
variants.code_sketch:
val payment = LinkValue(base / "payments" / order.paymentId,
                        rel = "payment".some,
                        `type` = MediaType.application.json.some)
Ok(dto).putHeaders(Link(payment))          // producer: RFC 8288 Link header
// consumer: resp.headers.get[Link] -> dereference with the client
val paymentUri = resp.headers.get[Link].get.values.head.uri
client.expect[Payment](paymentUri)         // IO[Payment]
pitfalls: http4s operates on typed URIs and Uri.fromString is total (Either), but the header model changed shape across versions: v0.20's Link(uri, rel, title, type) case class became Link(values: NonEmptyList[LinkValue]) from v0.21 - code and stored API contracts written against the old tuple-style Link break on upgrade, so pin the http4s series wherever the Link header is part of the contract.

The dereference is deferred and effectful: client.expect[Payment](link.uri) runs when the IO is run, not where it is built - a leaked or duplicated IO dereferences the link twice or never, and unmanaged fibers chasing link chains are the Scala analogue of unbounded link-following; bound depth and time budgets inside the effect, not around it.
